## Failure list (`holdout_iter2`, generated; every non-perfect question)

### w04 (synonym): Which site can generate the most electricity, and how much?

- expected (answered): Dunmere Flats, 410 MW
- got (answered): Dunmere Flats, an offshore wind site, has the largest installed capacity at 410 MW, so it can generate the most electricity (installed capacity is the maximum generation capability).
- judge: correct: The answer matches the reference: Dunmere Flats with 410 MW, with only additional correct context.
- retrieval: gold pages [4, 5], first gold rank 7, top 5: p6-f1, p1-x1, p6-x1, p2-x1, p3-t1
- unverified citations: 0 of 2
- oracle context (p4-x1, p4-t1, p5-x1): answered, judge correct: Dunmere Flats has the largest installed capacity at 410 MW, so it can generate the most electricity (subject to its 93.6% availability in 2025).

### w07 (synonym): Which sites are underperforming enough to trigger a performance review?

- expected (answered): Brannock Ridge (91.2%), Fenwick (89.7%) and Greyfell (90.4%) are below 92%. The review needs two consecutive years below 92%; the report gives only 2025.
- got (refused): The document states that a performance review is triggered when a site's availability is below 92% in two consecutive years, but only 2025 availability figures are provided, so it cannot be determined which sites meet the two-year condition. In 2025 alone, Fenwick (89.7%) and Greyfell (90.4%) were below 92%, but the prior year's availability is not given.
- judge: partial: Correctly notes the two-consecutive-year requirement and lists Fenwick and Greyfell, but omits Brannock Ridge (91.2%) which was also below 92% in 2025.
- retrieval: gold pages [4, 5], first gold rank 1, top 5: p4-x1, p1-x1, p2-x1, p3-t1, p3-x1
- unverified citations: 0 of 3
- oracle context (p4-x1, p4-t1, p5-x1): answered, judge correct: A site triggers review when availability is below 92% in two consecutive years, but the excerpts only provide 2025 availability, so it cannot be confirmed that any site triggers a review. Three sites were below 92% in 2025: Brannock Ridge (91.2%), Fenwick (89.7%) and Greyfell (90.4%). Prior-year availability is missing, so whether they met the two-consecutive-year condition is unknown.
